question.worked_solution:
To determine whether the line $y=3x+2$ intersects the parabola $y={x}^{2}+5x+k,$ we need to solve the following system of equations for the two curves:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y={x}^{2}+5x+k \\ y=3x+2\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and writing in standard form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+5x+k & =3x+2 \\ {x}^{2}+2x+(k-2) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve this equation using the quadratic formula with $a=1,$ $b=2,$ and $c=k-2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{(2)^{2}-4(1)(k-2)}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{4-4k+8}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2\pm \sqrt{12-4k}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the line and parabola do not intersect, our quadratic equation must have no real solutions; hence, the expression inside the square root must be negative. Setting up and solving this inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}12-4k & <0 \\ -4k & <-12 \\ k & >3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range of possible values of $k$ is $k>3.$
